clues: Kit stood exactly three places ahead of Ivan.
Whoever stood third in line was either Ivan or Rosa.
hints: Look at clue 1. In a line of only four people, how much room does a gap of exactly three places need?
Clue 1 is an exact gap, so count. Try Kit in each place and see where Ivan would have to stand.
Only first and fourth are three places apart, so Kit was first and Ivan fourth. Clue 2 then gives third place to Rosa.

solution.key_idea: In a line of four, only first and fourth are three places apart, so clue 1 puts Kit first and Ivan fourth.
steps: Clue 2 says the third customer was Ivan or Rosa, so neither Faye nor Kit stood third.
By clue 1, Kit stood exactly three places ahead of Ivan. In a line of four, only first and fourth are three places apart.
So Kit was first in line and Ivan was fourth.
By clue 2, the third customer was Ivan or Rosa. Ivan was fourth, so Rosa was third.
Faye was left with second place, right where the bill was found. The five dollars were Faye's.
solution.epilogue: The five had slipped from Faye's pocket while she dug out coins for a double scoop. Ada returned it the next morning, and Faye bought the scooper a lemonade in thanks.

tip: Count an exact gap on your fingers. In a short line, a big gap has very few places to fit.
